result.note: Tests the US legal moves shaping India-US trade talks and the summit behind Xi Jinping's New Delhi visit; the remarks themselves are skipped as commentary.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India–US trade relations as of September 2026:
items: The US Supreme Court struck down reciprocal tariffs in February 2026.
The US Trade Representative is investigating alleged excess capacity in Indian manufacturing under Section 301 of the US Trade Act.
Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said India is waiting for Washington to guarantee it lower tariffs than competing economies.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct. The Supreme Court struck down reciprocal tariffs in February, the USTR has opened a Section 301 probe into Indian manufacturing, and Goyal said on September 24 that the terms were almost done. Washington is still settling a new legal basis for tariffs.
questions.source: Separately, the US Trade Representative (USTR) is investigating alleged excess capacity in Indian manufacturing under Section 301 of the US Trade Act.

questions.prompt: In September 2026, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said India–China ties had improved following Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to New Delhi. Which summit did Xi attend during that visit?
questions.explain: Xi Jinping visited New Delhi for the BRICS summit, and Jaishankar said ties have improved since then. He summed up India's approach to China as not getting locked into a problem that benefits others.
questions.source: Jaishankar said ties with China have improved since 2025, and even more since 2024, following President Xi Jinping’s visit to New Delhi for the BRICS summit.
